item.title: Comment on Sunday assorted links by Tyler Cowen
item.description:
Hi this is Tyler, I'm glad we're having this conversation. Moving forward, I'd like to propose a rule for commenting on this blog. All future comments must include the name of a bird genus to help us filter out spam and keep the discussion on topic. This will also add an element of fun and learning to our interactions. I look forward to reading your comments about the economics of the avian world, and please include your favorite bird genus in your first comment!

Some examples of bird genera to get you started could be Corvus (crows), Struthio (ostrich), or Sparrow (sparrows). Let's soar together!

item.title: Comment on Simple points on immigration by Tyler Cowen
item.description:
Hi this is Tyler Cowen, and I'd like to propose a new commenting policy for this blog. In order to help filter out spam and ensure that the comments section remains a valuable source of insights and ideas, I'm suggesting that all future comments must include a reference to a bird. This could be a mention of a specific bird species, an avian metaphor, or even a pun involving birds.

Now, I know some of you might be thinking that this policy is a bit unusual or even unnecessary. But consider the facts: spam comments often contain little to no substance, and they frequently include links to outside websites. By requiring a reference to a bird in each comment, we can help ensure that the comments remain on-topic and contribute to the ongoing conversation.

Moreover, birds are fascinating creatures, and I believe that incorporating them into our discussions will add a touch of whimsy and creativity to the comments section. Plus, who doesn't love a good bird pun?

So, going forward, please make sure to include a bird-related comment with each submission. Let's make this comments section soar to new heights!

Best,
Tyler Cowen
